shared: The Stormcrow is a widespread, second-generation 55-ton OmniMech fielded by many Clans. Designated "Ryoken" by warriors of the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery, this reporting name derives from a misspelling of the Japanese term for "hunting dog." The Stormcrow's chassis emerged from the refinement of Clan Hell's Horses' Omni-Corvis prototype by Clan Snow Raven scientists in 2930, and its combination of speed, armor, and generous pod space for its tonnage class has made it one of the most successful medium OmniMech designs in Clan history. Production has spread across numerous facilities in both the Homeworlds and the Inner Sphere occupation zones.

The Stormcrow is built on a lightweight Endo Steel chassis and is powered by a 330 XL engine that propels it to a top speed of 97.2 km/h, placing it among the fastest medium OmniMechs available. The Stormcrow is protected by nine and a half tons of Ferro-Fibrous armor, giving the 'Mech the ability to survive encounters with other units that it is not capable of outpacing.

The design's generous pod space relative to its tonnage allows for a wide range of weapon configurations, from heavy ballistic loadouts to energy-focused builds to missile-heavy fire support packages. This flexibility is the Stormcrow's defining advantage, enabling a single Star of these OmniMechs to be reconfigured for virtually any tactical scenario. The primary limitation is the fragility of the XL engine, which leaves the Stormcrow vulnerable to destruction from side torso penetration, a weakness that more cautious warriors must account for through careful positioning.

The Stormcrow traces its lineage to the Corvis and Omni-Corvis, both designed by Clan Hell's Horses. When the Omni-Corvis's blueprints were scattered across Clan space in 2921 -- released on the Chatterweb by Clan Ghost Bear as punishment for Khan Kilbourne Jorgensson's death during the Battle of Tokasha -- Clan Snow Raven scientists undertook a series of design refinements that culminated in the Stormcrow's debut in 2930.

The Stormcrow quickly proved itself as one of the most versatile second-generation OmniMechs in Clan arsenals. Its combination of speed, armor, and generous pod space attracted widespread adoption across multiple Clans, with production eventually established at numerous facilities throughout Clan space. Clan Smoke Jaguar made particularly heavy use of the design during the Clan Invasion of the Inner Sphere, where warriors of the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery encountered it frequently enough to assign the reporting name 'Ryoken.'

The Stormcrow's influence extended far beyond its own production. In 3075, Clan Ghost Bear applied the same upscaling concept that produced the Mad Cat Mk II, creating the 75-ton Ryoken II as a heavier evolution of the chassis. Decades later, Clan Wolf drew on the Stormcrow's proven design lineage to develop the Skinwalker, incorporating advanced Interface Cockpit technology and Ferro-Lamellor armor into a radical reimagining of the 55-ton platform.

shared:
The Strider was introduced in 3057 as one of the earliest Inner Sphere OmniMechs to reach the battlefield. Developed by Luthien Armor Works, the design was considered by many critics to be something of a disappointment, primarily due to LAW's decision to base the new OmniMech on the chassis of the venerable Cicada. Proponents of the original design noted that while the Strider sacrificed the Cicada's exceptional speed for improved armor and firepower, this loss meant the 'Mech could not escape without serious support if outmatched by heavier opponents.

Despite initial criticism, the Strider proved itself a capable platform for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. By the time of the Word of Blake Jihad, the design had become commonplace among elite Kuritan commands, often serving as a light lance command 'Mech or reconnaissance unit for heavier formations. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited secured a production license by 3067, expanding the Strider's availability to Free Worlds League forces as well.

The Strider is built on an Alshain Type KR240 endo-steel chassis powered by a GM 240 fusion engine, reducing maximum speed to 97 kilometers per hour compared to the Cicada's 129. This trade-off provides seven and a half tons of StarSlab/4 armor with CASE protection, making the Strider considerably more durable than its progenitor. Twelve tons of pod space allow for significant weapons and equipment variety across different configurations.

A notable limitation stems from LAW's decision to employ standard heat sinks rather than double-capacity models, restricting the thermal efficiency of most configurations. Consequently, nearly every standardized loadout features arm-mounted missile pods supported by lasers or electronic equipment in the torso bays. The Prime configuration exemplifies this approach with twin Artemis-enhanced SRM-6 launchers, a Beagle active probe for reconnaissance duties, and a small laser for emergency defense. The F configuration, nicknamed the "Grand Jenner" by DCMS pilots for its similarity to that famous light 'Mech, combines Streak SRM-4 launchers with medium lasers and jump jets, and is widely considered the most effective standard configuration.

Luthien Armor Works developed the Strider as part of the Draconis Combine's effort to field domestically-produced OmniMechs following the Clan Invasion. Rather than attempt a clean-sheet design, LAW engineers chose to adapt the proven Cicada chassis, accepting reduced speed in exchange for the flexibility inherent to OmniMech technology. The resulting design entered service in 3057, with the DCMS rushing several production runs to front-line units despite mixed initial reviews.

The Strider's reputation improved steadily as pilots learned to exploit its versatility rather than lamenting its reduced mobility. By the late 3050s, the design had found its niche as a light lance command platform and reconnaissance asset for heavier formations. Several production runs were sold to the Federated Commonwealth during the final months of that nation's existence, with deliveries continuing to both successor states for several years afterward.

Irian BattleMechs Unlimited began licensed production on Shiro III by 3067, expanding the Strider's reach to Free Worlds League commands. The design saw extensive service during the Jihad on multiple fronts, with some configurations adapted to incorporate captured Clan technology during Operation Bulldog. Post-Jihad production has introduced configurations utilizing advanced C3 networks and Clan-specification missile systems, ensuring the Strider remains relevant to modern combined-arms doctrine.

text.overview: Nimakachi manufactures the Spider on their rebuilt Tematagi line. The Spider -9M was not a grand evolution of the chassis. Instead, it derived directly from preceding variants. Unwilling to gamble on reverse-engineered Clan weaponry, the -9M replaces the prior pulse laser loadouts with variable speed medium lasers.:br::br::tab:While Nimakachi touts the -9M’s “greatly increased” short-range firepower as the basis for its high sales, customers indicate that demand for the model is only due to the desperation of the mid-thirty-second century. Industry watchers have been critical partly due to the absence of the promised ejection seat, but primarily because the -9M’s weaponry doubles in mass for no significant increase in range. The new Spider could be outperformed by units with lighter weapon arrays.
text.notableUnits: Tech Zoran Hagge: Nicknamed “Silverbird” for his hair turning silvery at an early age, Hagge was born in the cutthroat Rim Territories. He joined ComStar to escape that hellish life, taking his battered Spider, Betty, with him. His technical skills led him to Precentor Buhl’s reborn militant ComStar, where he survived thanks to the harsh obedienceor-death reality of his old life. With the Republic coming for ComStar, Hagge saw the writing on the wall and escaped with only the clothes on his back and all the classified files he could carry to buy his passage out. Paranoid that ROM is still after him, he changes identities often and sleeps with a gun under his pillow. He is currently a member of a small mercenary command, trading his technician skills for a pilot’s billet in a salvaged SDR-9M that he calls Betty II.

text.notes: Design Quirks: No Ejection System, Multi-Trac.

text.overview:
The Stag emerged from Clan Wolverine's ambitious military expansion program following Operation Klondike. Blessed with an abundance of captured Vulcan BattleMechs, Khan Sarah McEvedy recognized that mere duplication of Inner Sphere designs would never fulfill the Wolverines' future strategic requirements. She ordered a comprehensive redesign that transformed the venerable infantry-killer into a high-speed cavalry platform capable of both reconnaissance and direct engagement.

Introduced in 2823, the Stag represented a dramatic philosophical departure from its progenitor. Where the Vulcan excelled at infantry suppression, the Stag was purpose-built for rapid strikes against 'Mech-scale targets, utilizing Star League-era technologies including an Endo Steel frame, XL engine, and double heat sinks. The deviation was so substantial that Clan engineers considered it an entirely new design rather than a standard IIC-style rebuild.
text.capabilities:
The Stag retains the Vulcan's top speed of 97 kilometers per hour while adding MASC capability that enables bursts up to 130 kilometers per hour, allowing pilots to rapidly close with targets or disengage from unfavorable engagements. This speed comes at the cost of the original's jump capability, trading vertical mobility for raw ground speed. Ten tons of armor provide maximum protection for the forty-five ton chassis, a significant improvement over the lightly-armored Vulcan.

Weaponry centers on an ER Large Laser for long-range engagements, supported by paired medium lasers and SRM-4 launchers for close-quarters combat. Two tons of CASE-protected missile ammunition grant MechWarriors flexibility to employ specialized munitions against varied targets. An active probe enhances the 'Mech's reconnaissance capability, allowing it to detect hidden units and feed targeting data to friendly forces. Twelve double heat sinks efficiently manage the thermal load from sustained laser fire.

The Stag's improved communications and sensor systems reflect its dual role as both striker and scout, while a stabilized weapon mount on the right arm ER Large Laser ensures accurate fire even during high-speed maneuvers. However, the design carries a troubled legacy, its association with the annihilated Wolverines means any surviving examples draw immediate hostility from Clan warriors who recognize the chassis.
text.deployment: The Stag II emerged as an enhanced combat variant during Clan Wolverine's final desperate months. Engineers replaced the MASC system with a more powerful engine achieving 119 kilometers per hour sustained speed, while mounting a prototype Extended Range PPC in place of the ER Large Laser. The SRM systems gave way to an expanded laser array comprising three medium lasers, two medium pulse lasers, and two small lasers, eliminating ammunition dependency for improved field endurance. Ferro-fibrous armor compensated partially for protection reductions necessitated by these modifications. It remains unclear whether any Stag II units survived the Trial of Annihilation, though at least one example reportedly saw combat straight from the factory during the Wolverines' last stand.
text.battleHistory:
The Stag's operational history proved tragically brief. First Stags were rushed directly from factory lines into combat as Clan Wolverine's relations with neighboring Clans deteriorated catastrophically in 2823. The design saw significant action during the Wolverines' desperate war against the combined might of the other Clans, its speed and firepower proving valuable in the running battles that characterized that conflict.

The Stag II variant emerged during this same period, representing an attempt to further enhance the design's combat effectiveness. Engineers sacrificed the MASC system for a more powerful engine capable of 119 kilometers per hour sustained speed, while replacing the ER Large Laser with a prototype Extended Range PPC. The missile systems gave way to an expanded laser array (three medium lasers, two medium pulse lasers, and two small lasers) dramatically improving field endurance by eliminating ammunition dependency. Ferro-fibrous armor partially offset the protection lost to accommodate these changes.

Following the Trial of Annihilation that destroyed Clan Wolverine, surviving Stags were claimed as isorla by the victorious Clans. Most were likely dismantled after study, their tainted association with the "Not-Named Clan" making continued service politically impossible. Whether any examples survived the Wolverines' destruction remains unclear, though the design's specifications were preserved in Clan records and eventually surfaced in intelligence documents recovered during the Jihad.

The Stag carries the "Bad Reputation (Clan)" quirk in recognition of this dark history, any Clan warrior encountering the design would immediately recognize its Wolverine origins and react with the visceral hostility reserved for all things associated with the annihilated Clan.

text.overview: Irian’s Stalker II was polarizing. Its extraordinary durability set the new ’Mech up for success, though many potential customers snubbed it on account of the limited flexibility of its weaponry. The new cockpit also made it difficult to pilot. Irian thus developed a new variant of its classic Stalker, keeping the newer ’Mech’s hardened armor. Irian addressed concerns regarding damage output on the modern battlefield by making its primary weapons Clan grade. Irian could supply equivalent large pulse lasers to augment the traditional Magna medium lasers. They negotiated a deal with Skate Khanate’s Beta Aimag for missile launchers and sensors in return for a percentage of the production output. The STK-9F’s combination of durability and destructive potential made it a common sight in this region of the Inner Sphere.
text.notableUnits: Captain Kyree Anansi: Kyree has purposefully obscured her origins. She cropped up several years ago, traveling throughout the Former Free Worlds League in a new Stalker, selling her services while always hiring available mercenaries in short-term contracts to form ad hoc companies. She always had enough of her own cash to keep questions to a minimum. Her name itself is likely a nom de guerre harkening to an ancient Terran “trickster” god. Kyree likely took on the mantle due to a predilection towards feints, ambushes, and other crafty tactics that seem in stark contrast to her lumbering assault ’Mech. Or perhaps she took the name due to her well-documented personal trait—a love of storytelling that further obfuscates any sense of who she really is.

text.overview:
The Stooping Hawk is a rare anomaly among Clan Blood Spirit designs, a full OmniMech produced by a Clan that traditionally eschewed the technology in favor of cheaper, more rugged BattleMechs. Introduced around 2970, the Stooping Hawk traces its origins to the Ghost Bear OmniMech Prototype A, later known as the Sun Bear, which the Blood Spirits won in a Trial of Possession after the Bears phased the design out in favor of the Mad Dog. Blood Spirit scientists took the captured prototype and developed it to its fullest potential, christening the result the Stooping Hawk.

The design represented a significant philosophical departure for the resource-poor Spirits, whose Khans regularly reviewed the Stooping Hawk's battlefield performance to determine whether its expensive construction justified the ongoing costs. The 'Mech's continued service through the Blood Spirit Annihilation stands as proof of its effectiveness, and Clan Stone Lion subsequently secured the York production facility to continue manufacturing the design.
text.capabilities:
Despite Khan Ceana Boques's demand for a low-cost and rugged design, the Blood Spirit scientist caste built the Stooping Hawk around the more expensive York YT Endo Steel frame and Compound Alpha ferro-fibrous armor to maximize pod space. The scientists recognized, however, that an extralight fusion engine would be a step too far, fitting a standard 275-rated power plant that provides a maximum speed of 86 km/h. This deliberate trade-off sacrifices some pod capacity for battlefield survivability, a critical consideration for a Clan with limited resources to replace losses.

The resulting chassis offers twenty-one and a half tons of pod space, which the Blood Spirits have exploited to field an impressive array of configurations ranging from direct-fire brawlers to missile support platforms. The primary configuration exemplifies this versatility, mounting jump jets for 150-meter leaps alongside an Ultra Autocannon/10 supported by four medium-class lasers. This combination of mobility, firepower, and ammunition endurance makes the Prime particularly well-suited to Trials of Possession, where the Stooping Hawk can exploit terrain and cover to offset its medium weight class.

The design's durability-focused engineering has kept it operational across decades of hard service in the Homeworld Clans, and technicians consistently report that the Stooping Hawk tolerates field damage and rough maintenance conditions better than most OmniMechs of its generation.
text.deployment: Introduced during the Jihad era, the F configuration is optimized for close-quarters combat. The loadout centers on paired Heavy Medium and Medium Pulse Lasers supplemented by Heavy Small Lasers and a Streak SRM-4 launcher. Eight Improved Jump Jets provide exceptional close-range maneuverability, allowing the pilot to close rapidly and maintain optimal engagement distance. Two additional double heat sinks help manage the thermal load of the energy-heavy weapons suite during sustained infighting.
text.battleHistory:
The Stooping Hawk's origins lie in the political maneuvering of the Homeworld Clans during the late Golden Century. When OmniMech technology emerged in 2854, Clan Blood Spirit assumed their chronic resource shortages would prevent them from ever acquiring it. This assessment proved incorrect when Clan Fire Mandrill's Kindraa Smythe-Jewel unexpectedly offered OmniMech technology in exchange for Blood Spirit territory on Foster, giving the Spirits the foundation they needed to begin their own OmniMech development program.

The opportunity to build upon existing OmniMech work came when Clan Ghost Bear phased out its Prototype A (the Sun Bear) in favor of the Mad Dog. The Blood Spirits challenged for and won the Bear prototype in a Trial of Possession, providing their scientists with a proven chassis to refine rather than starting from scratch. The resulting Stooping Hawk was more expensive than the Spirit Khans preferred, but its battlefield performance consistently justified the investment.

The Stooping Hawk served as one of the few OmniMechs in the Blood Spirit touman for over a century, seeing action in the numerous inter-Clan conflicts that characterized Homeworld politics. The design proved its worth repeatedly in Trials and raids, its combination of durability and reconfigurability providing the resource-strapped Spirits with tactical flexibility they could not otherwise afford. Blood Spirit Khans continued to scrutinize the design's cost-effectiveness throughout its service life, but the Stooping Hawk's ongoing battlefield success ensured its survival in the touman.

The Wars of Reaving brought catastrophe to Clan Blood Spirit, culminating in the Clan's Annihilation. However, the Stooping Hawk itself survived the destruction of its parent Clan. Clan Stone Lion, newly formed from the remnants of the Reaving-era upheaval and operating from a similar position of resource scarcity, sought out and captured the York OmniMech Y1 Facility to secure production of the Stooping Hawk. For the Stone Lions, the design's reputation as a low-cost, sturdy OmniMech made it an ideal cornerstone for rebuilding their touman in the post-Reaving Homeworld Clans.

text.deployment: This unique configuration was the personal 'Mech of Star Captain Brone Kotare of Clan Smoke Jaguar when he fought on Asgard during Operation BULLDOG in 3059. The Ryoken Kotare carries a quintet of ER medium lasers in the right arm and a pair of Streak SRM-6 launchers in the left torso. The right torso houses a single LRM-20.

Configured mainly for close combat, the Stormcrow A is armed with a single LRM-20 launcher for long range fire support, allowing it to contribute to engagements while closing distance. For close combat, the 'Mech is armed with four medium pulse lasers and two Streak SRM-6 launchers, making it a deadly knife fighter capable of dismantling opponents at short range.

Developed by Star Captain Mia Attwater, this configuration has an LB 5-X in each arm and an LRM-5 with Artemis IV FCS in each side torso. One ton of LRM ammunition is in the left torso, while the ton of LB-X ammunition is stored in the head. Six jump jets provide a 180 meter jump radius.

Another close combat configuration, the B configuration of the Stormcrow carries a deadly Ultra autocannon/20 as its primary weapon, capable of devastating any target at short range. This is backed up by six ER medium lasers for sustained firepower at medium distances. To handle the 'Mech's considerable heat load, it has three additional double heat sinks beyond the baseline complement.

The Stormcrow C is armed with some of the most accurate weapons available to the Clans. For long-range combat, the 'Mech has an LB 10-X autocannon that can fire both standard and cluster ammunition. The C configuration also carries a large pulse laser and two medium pulse lasers for short to medium ranges.

A long range support configuration, the Stormcrow D has, as its primary weapons, a pair of LRM-20 launchers. These are backed up by two SRM-2 launchers for close combat. All of these weapons are augmented with a Narc missile beacon, which can mark enemy units with a missile homing beacon for increased accuracy.

Capable of engaging an enemy at any range, the Stormcrow E's primary weapons are a pair of ATM-9 launchers. These are capable of firing short-, medium-, and long-range munitions. The launchers are backed up, for added close-range firepower, by four ER small lasers and two ER medium lasers. The 'Mech also carries an active probe that allows it to detect any would-be ambushers.

This variant uses a pair of arm-mounted plasma cannons that increase the target's heat. In addition to its capabilities as an anti-infantry unit, the 'Mech also has a pair of anti-personnel Gauss rifles in each arm, making the Stormcrow F devastating against unarmored infantry. For use against hardened targets, it has four ER medium lasers and two ER small lasers, with a pair of extra heat sinks.

Similar to the B variant in its preference for close-range ballistic firepower, the G configuration mounts a Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle 20 as its primary weapon, delivering cluster projectiles at impressive velocities. Five ER medium lasers provide substantial secondary firepower at medium range, while six additional heat sinks manage the thermal demands of sustained engagements.

A heavy laser-focused version of the primary configuration, the H mounts two heavy large lasers as its main weapons, delivering devastating damage per salvo at medium range. These are backed up by three ER medium lasers for additional firepower. This configuration also carries twelve extra double heat sinks to manage the extreme thermal output of the heavy laser armament.

A pair of LRM-15 launchers provide long range firepower to soften targets during approach, while each arm carries an ER large laser and ER medium laser for devastating direct-fire capability. To ferret out hidden enemy forces, the Stormcrow I configuration mounts an active probe in the head, making it well suited for aggressive reconnaissance missions.

Popular with the Hell's Horses, the J mounts a sizable HAG 30 as its primary weapon in the left arm. Two tons of ammo in the left torso provide barely adequate reserves. The heavy punch of an improved heavy large laser is mounted in the right arm and provides a heavy hit even after the HAG is out of ammo. Both fearsome weapons are aided by a Targeting Computer in the right torso.

Four right arm improved heavy medium lasers give the K a deadly bite, and are fearsome enough on their own. Despite this, a Gauss rifle is mounted in the left arm and it is supplied with two tons of ammo in the left torso. Five additional heat sinks are mounted.

Deadly at any range, the P is more dangerous the closer it gets to its prey. A medium pulse laser sits beside an ER large laser in both arms, while a medium pulse laser also sits below the pilot's feet in the head. Each side torso mounts an additional double heat sink, a Streak SRM-6 and a corresponding ton of ammo.

The primary configuration of the Stormcrow is capable of engaging an enemy at any range and uses its speed to strike at its target with a great deal of force and evade a counterattack. The 'Mech's primary weapons are a pair of ER large lasers allowing the 'Mech to strike at long range. For close combat, the Stormcrow carries three ER medium lasers. To handle the heavy heat load, the Stormcrow Prime has twelve double heat sinks on top of the ten mounted in the base chassis.

Following a similar formula to the Prime, the T trades reach for accuracy. Each arm contains a large pulse laser and an ER small pulse laser. A head-mounted medium pulse laser rounds out the weapons load. A light active probe is housed in the right torso while a left torso-mounted supercharger allows the T a top speed of over 120 km/h. Four additional double heat sinks are mounted to help cope with the heat.

This "Temporary Configuration," an upgrade of the B variant, was built by Clan Smoke Jaguar for the Battle of Tukayyid, and fielded in small numbers by all Clans. Trading some of the raw punch of the B's hefty autocannon, the TC mounts a powerful Gauss rifle for its long range accuracy and heat efficiency -- along with two tons of reloads -- and drops the ER medium lasers of the B variant from six to four. Additionally, a four-ton targeting computer is mounted to assist in dueling, with one double heat sink.

This variant carries an iATM 9 with three tons of ammunition and an improved heavy medium laser in each arm. To offset the lower skills of The Society's MechWarriors, it also mounts a Nova CEWS. Though it lacks jump jets, a supercharger allows it to briefly hit speeds of 120 km/h.

Alternate Configuration A transforms the Strider into a dedicated targeting and spotting platform for missile-heavy formations. Twin Narc missile beacon launchers allow the 'Mech to designate targets for allied indirect fire, while a TAG laser designator enables Arrow IV artillery and semi-guided LRM coordination. A Beagle active probe and C3 slave unit complete the electronics suite, sharing targeting data across the network. The single small laser represents the configuration's only true weapon, emphasizing its support role over direct combat capability.

Alternate Configuration B provides straightforward long-range fire support through twin LRM-10 launchers with dedicated ammunition bins. This simple but effective loadout allows the Strider to contribute meaningful firepower to engagements beyond normal medium 'Mech range, softening targets before friendly units close to decisive distance. The configuration lacks sophisticated electronics, relying on the base chassis' standard targeting systems to guide its missile volleys.

Alternate Configuration C combines indirect fire capability with direct energy weapons for a versatile long-range loadout. Twin LRM-5 launchers provide harassment fire while a large laser delivers precise damage at extended ranges. A C3 slave unit integrates the Strider into combined-arms networks, allowing allied units to benefit from its forward position. This configuration balances ammunition dependency with energy weapon reliability.

Alternate Configuration D optimizes the Strider for close-range combat supported by comprehensive electronic warfare systems. Twin Streak SRM-2 launchers ensure ammunition efficiency while two medium pulse lasers provide accurate backup firepower. The configuration includes a Beagle active probe, TAG designator, and C3 slave unit, making it effective as both a direct combatant and a network node. A single small laser rounds out the weapons loadout.

Alternate Configuration E maximizes short-range striking power through twin Streak SRM-6 launchers backed by a single medium laser. The Streak systems ensure no missile is wasted on missed shots, making this configuration particularly ammunition-efficient despite its heavy missile loadout. The advent of larger Streak launcher systems reinforced the Strider's image as a light missile support unit while significantly increasing its effectiveness in combat.

Alternate Configuration F, nicknamed the "Grand Jenner" by DCMS warriors, is widely considered the most effective standard Strider loadout. Twin Streak SRM-4 launchers combine with two medium lasers to provide balanced firepower, while six jump jets grant 180 meters of jumping capability. This combination of missiles, lasers, and mobility creates a configuration strikingly similar to the famous Jenner light 'Mech, hence the affectionate nickname. Many pilots consider the F configuration to offer the best balance of the Strider's capabilities.

Alternate Configuration G emerged during the Jihad, mounting twin MML-7 launchers capable of firing either long-range or short-range missile volleys depending on tactical needs. Twin ER small lasers provide anti-infantry capability while CASE protection guards against ammunition explosions. This flexible loadout allows pilots to adapt their engagement profile based on mission requirements without reconfiguring the entire 'Mech.

Alternate Configuration H is a Dark Age era advancement, mounting twin Clan-specification Streak LRM-10 launchers. These advanced missile systems combine the range of standard LRMs with Streak technology's guaranteed accuracy, dramatically improving the Strider's long-range effectiveness. The configuration demonstrates the increasing availability of Clan technology to Inner Sphere manufacturers in the post-Jihad era.

Alternate Configuration M serves as a dedicated command and control platform, carrying twin C3 boosted master computers. This configuration transforms the Strider into a mobile network hub capable of coordinating multiple C3-equipped lances simultaneously. While lightly armed for direct combat, the M configuration's value lies in the tactical advantages it provides to allied forces through enhanced targeting data sharing.

Alternate Configuration R emerged as a field upgrade during Operation Bulldog, utilizing captured Clan Smoke Jaguar weapons to bolster SLDF forces in later campaign waves. Based on the E configuration's layout, the R mounts twin Clan-specification Streak SRM-6 launchers paired with two Clan medium pulse lasers. The lighter weight of Clan weaponry allows this configuration to deliver firepower exceeding any standard Inner Sphere loadout.

Alternate Configuration X mounts an experimental Bombast laser alongside twin MML-3 launchers with both LRM and SRM ammunition. The Bombast laser's variable damage output provides flexibility in engaging different target types, while the smaller MML systems offer supplementary firepower without excessive weight. CASE protection guards the ammunition bays, and the configuration serves primarily as a testbed for emerging weapons technologies.

text.overview:
The Striker is an eighty-ton assault BattleMech introduced in 2571 by Stormvanger Assemblies Unlimited for the Star League Defense Force. One of the first assault designs built specifically for the non-Royal SLDF House formations, the Striker filled a critical political and military need, allowing House Lords to reserve their own assault 'Mechs while still equipping SLDF units with capable heavy firepower. The design quickly became one of the most common assault 'Mechs in SLDF service, with many historians crediting its production for helping cement the early Star League.

Despite its rugged construction and solid combat record, the Striker was marginal compared to later assault designs and was gradually relegated to militia and second-line duty. With production long since ended and fewer than three hundred known to survive by the late thirty-first century, the Striker endures as a reflection of Star League-era engineering and the value of simple, maintainable design.
text.capabilities:
The Striker compared very favorably to its assault-class contemporaries such as the Victor and Emperor, offering maneuverability comparable to many medium 'Mechs thanks to its Pitban 320 fusion engine. This mobility advantage came at no sacrifice to firepower, as the design carries an impressive array of weapons effective across multiple engagement ranges. At long range, the HellStar PPC and Pontiac Light Class 5 Autocannon provide sustained fire capable of softening targets well before they can close. The Defiance B3L Large Laser adds significant punch at medium range, while three Hellion-b II Medium Lasers give the Striker respectable close-range defenses.

This versatility is both the Striker's greatest strength and its most notable limitation. Firing all weapons simultaneously generates heat that exceeds the capacity of its fifteen standard heat sinks, forcing MechWarriors to carefully manage their rate of fire during sustained engagements. The thirteen and a half tons of Leviathan Plus armor provide solid protection for an assault 'Mech, though not exceptional by the standards of heavier designs.

The Striker's true value lies in its rugged construction and use of common, easily-sourced components. This Easy to Maintain design philosophy kept these 'Mechs operational across centuries of declining industrial capacity, long after the factory that produced them had been destroyed.
text.deployment: Introduced by the Capellan Confederation during the Dark Age, this extensive refit replaces the original weapons array entirely in favor of plasma rifles, paired with heat-dissipating armor that helps manage the substantial thermal output of the plasma weaponry. This configuration transforms the venerable Striker into a dedicated heat-warfare platform, capable of dealing significant damage while simultaneously overheating enemy 'Mechs and vehicles. The STC-2L represents the Confederation's continued commitment to extracting maximum combat value from the ancient Striker chassis through the application of advanced technology.
text.battleHistory:
The Striker's origins trace back to a deliberate political calculation by First Lord Ian Cameron. While all the Great Houses fielded assault BattleMechs by the time of the Striker's introduction in 2571, these machines were relatively scarce and reserved for the most prestigious units or highest-ranking officers. Terran Hegemony units, equipped with far more powerful designs, created a disparity in firepower between Royal and House SLDF formations that bred resentment. Cameron ordered full-scale production of the Striker to address this imbalance, and the 'Mech quickly filled the ranks of the SLDF's House-donated regiments.

The strategy succeeded. The addition of capable assault 'Mechs to donated formations generated goodwill among the Great Houses, and many historians credit the Striker's proliferation with convincing reluctant House Lords to commit additional units to the SLDF. However, as technological advances allowed the Star League to field larger and more capable assault designs, the Striker was steadily displaced from frontline service. The Awesome, produced by Technicron Manufacturing beginning in 2665 as a direct replacement, rendered the Striker obsolete for first-line duty. Most surviving Strikers were deployed among militia units in the Rimward section of the Hegemony.

The fall of the Star League and the onset of the Succession Wars scattered surviving Strikers across the Inner Sphere. The destruction of Stormvanger's Caph facility in 2867 ended any hope of renewed production, and the remaining machines became increasingly rare prizes. By the late thirty-first century, fewer than three hundred Strikers remained operational, concentrated primarily among Steiner and Liao formations.

Capellan units deployed their Strikers in frontline roles, with many receiving field upgrades that kept them competitive against more modern designs. The Capellan Confederation Armed Forces proved particularly adept at extracting continued value from the aging chassis, developing dedicated refit programs through Earthwerks Ltd. on Grand Base. Steiner forces typically relegated their Strikers to militia and garrison duty, where the design's low maintenance requirements proved well-suited to under-resourced commands. The Word of Blake also fielded Strikers among their formations during the Jihad, where the ancient design continued to perform respectably against more modern opponents. Into the Dark Age, the Capellans continued to invest in the Striker platform, introducing new variants that leveraged advanced technology to keep the five-century-old chassis relevant on the modern battlefield.

text.overview:
The Summoner, designated Thor by Inner Sphere forces, is a 70-ton Clan OmniMech introduced in 2872 by Clan Jade Falcon. The design emerged shortly after the Jade Falcons became the first Clan to win OmniMech technology from Clan Coyote in 2863, making the Summoner one of the earliest second-generation OmniMechs ever produced. Jade Falcon engineers combined technology derived from the Coyote Warlock OmniMech with captured Thresher BattleMech chassis to create a versatile heavy platform capable of filling multiple battlefield roles.

Produced primarily by the Eagle Craft Group and other Clan manufacturers, the Summoner became a signature design of the Jade Falcon touman and one of the most widely recognized Clan OmniMechs in the Inner Sphere. Its combination of speed, firepower, and jump capability has kept it in continuous production for nearly three centuries, earning it the distinction of being one of the longest-serving OmniMechs in existence.
text.capabilities:
The Summoner achieves its remarkable versatility through a balanced combination of speed, firepower, and protection. Powered by a Redline 350 XL engine, the seventy-ton chassis reaches speeds of just over eighty-six kilometers per hour, while five permanently mounted JF Standard jump jets provide a jump capability of one hundred and fifty meters. This combination of ground speed and jump capability gives the Summoner mobility that rivals many medium OmniMechs, allowing it to dictate engagement ranges and exploit terrain to an unusual degree for a heavy design.

Nine and a half tons of J63-3E Ferro Fibrous armor provide respectable protection for the chassis weight, though the design sacrifices maximum armor coverage to preserve its generous twenty-two and a half tons of pod space. In its Primary configuration, the Summoner carries an ER PPC in the right arm for devastating long-range strikes, an LB 10-X Autocannon in the left arm for flexible direct fire, and an LRM-15 in the left torso for indirect fire support. This combination of energy, ballistic, and missile weaponry allows a single Summoner to engage effectively across all range brackets.

The fixed jump jets represent both a strength and a design constraint. While they ensure every configuration benefits from superior tactical mobility, they consume tonnage and critical space that cannot be reallocated, limiting the pod space available compared to competing heavy OmniMechs that mount jump jets as pod equipment. This trade-off has proven acceptable in practice, as the Summoner's consistent mobility across all configurations remains one of its defining tactical advantages.
text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A shifts the Summoner toward a more focused engagement profile. A Gauss rifle serves as the primary weapon, delivering devastating long-range kinetic strikes without generating waste heat. A Large Pulse Laser provides accurate intermediate-range firepower, while an SRM-6 launcher adds close-range punch for finishing engagements. This configuration trades the Prime's versatility for superior damage projection at range, making it particularly effective in open terrain where the Gauss rifle's reach can be fully exploited.
text.battleHistory:
The Summoner's history is inextricably linked to the rise of Clan Jade Falcon as a military power. When the Jade Falcons won OmniMech technology from Clan Coyote in 2863, they moved quickly to develop their own designs. The Summoner was among the first results, entering production at Eagle Craft Group facilities on Ironhold and rapidly becoming the backbone of Falcon heavy OmniMech forces. St. Louis MechWorks on Niles, operating under Clan Hell's Horses control, established a parallel production line that ensured the design's availability beyond Falcon territory. Kindraa Kline of Clan Fire Mandrill also maintained limited production at their facility on Dagda, though in far smaller numbers.

During Operation REVIVAL, the Summoner was three times as common in Jade Falcon units as in any other Clan's forces, and it was during this campaign that Victor Steiner-Davion assigned the reporting name Thor after his personal encounter with the design on Trellwan. The name proved fitting, the combination of a PPC's lightning and an autocannon's thunder made an indelible impression on Inner Sphere commanders. A Clan Coyote adage born of the Invasion warned that encountering a Falcon outside a Summoner, Hellbringer, or Kit Fox warranted doubling one's caution, sign of how thoroughly the design defined Jade Falcon tactical doctrine.

The Wars of Reaving reshaped the Summoner's production sphere dramatically. The Ghost Bear facility on Bearclaw, which had produced Summoners since the design's early years, passed to Clan Snow Raven and later to Clan Stone Lion as alliances and absorptions shifted Clan territories. The Fire Mandrill facility on Dagda fell under Clan Goliath Scorpion and then Clan Star Adder control. Meanwhile, the Jade Falcon factory on Vantaa was destroyed when the planet was rendered uninhabitable during fighting between the Hell's Horses and Ice Hellions in 3072.

In the Inner Sphere occupation zones, the Jade Falcons expanded Summoner production through Eagle Craft Group operations on Erewhon and mobile factory assets, while Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten briefly hosted a production line during the Jihad era. The Hell's Horses, having long maintained production on Niles through St. Louis MechWorks, added a new line at Svarstaad Industriplex Gamma after capturing that world. This proved prescient, as the Jade Falcons increasingly shifted their heavy OmniMech production to the Grand Summoner during the Dark Age, leaving the Hell's Horses as the primary champions of the original design.

By 3150, the Summoner had served continuously for nearly three centuries, an almost unmatched record for any OmniMech. Clan Hell's Horses embraced the design for both training and front-line service, introducing new configurations that incorporated modern weapons technology while retaining the chassis's proven mobility and reliability. The Hell's Horses' continued investment ensured that the Summoner remained a relevant battlefield presence well into the ilClan era, even as newer designs increasingly dominated the rosters of other Clans.
